theme.title: The 1970 Finals
theme.subtitle: Knicks vs Lakers
theme.recap: The 1970 Finals had a 60-foot buzzer-beater and Willis Reed's walk-out in Game 7, where Walt Frazier did the damage.

questions.prompt: The 1969–70 Knicks set what was then a single-season record winning streak. How long was it?

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: The Knicks had a then single-season NBA record 18 straight victories en route to 60–22 record

funFacts.text: That Knicks team also started the season at a record pace before Golden State broke its early-season mark decades later.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: They set the record for the best start in the first 24 games of a season at 23–1

funFacts.text: The Knicks went through Baltimore and Milwaukee before meeting the Lakers in the championship series.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: After defeating the Bullets in the Eastern Division semifinals and the Milwaukee Bucks in the Eastern Division finals

funFacts.text: Their title run later became the subject of the documentary When the Garden Was Eden.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Their journey was chronicled in various books and films, most recently in When the Garden was Eden

questions.prompt: Walt Frazier scored 36 points in Game 7 of the 1970 Finals. How many assists did he have?

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: took it from there, finishing with 36 points and 19 assists as the Knicks won the championship, 113–99.

funFacts.text: Clyde also registered six steals in the decider, showing how much of his masterpiece came on defense.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: tallying 36 points, seven rebounds, 19 assists, and six steals

funFacts.text: The Finals were the first to be broadcast nationally in full, with ABC calling the series.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: The 1970 NBA Finals were the first to be nationally televised in full, with ABC providing the coverage

funFacts.text: New Yorkers could not see the clincher live on local ABC television because the telecast was blacked out.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: the Knicks' victory in Game 7 was not seen live on broadcast TV in New York

questions.prompt: Willis Reed limped out for Game 7 of the 1970 Finals. How many minutes did he play?
questions.note: 27. He did not leave after his first two baskets, despite the legend.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Contrary to popular lore, he did not sit out after his first two baskets, but remained on the floor for 27 minutes

funFacts.text: Reed's entrance was so improbable because a torn thigh muscle had kept him out of the previous game.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Due to a severe thigh injury suffered in Game 5, a torn muscle that kept him out of Game 6

funFacts.text: He made New York's opening two baskets on his first two attempts, electrifying Madison Square Garden.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: he scored the Knicks' first two field goals on his first two shot attempts

funFacts.text: On defense, the injured Reed held Wilt Chamberlain to two makes on nine attempts while he was guarding him.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: limiting him to two shots made in nine attempts

questions.prompt: Jerry West forced overtime in Game 3 of the 1970 Finals with a buzzer-beater from how many feet?
questions.context: 1970 NBA Finals · Game 3 · at New York

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: hit a desperation buzzer-beating 60-foot shot to tie it at 102 and force OT

funFacts.text: West's miracle shot counted for only two because the NBA had not yet adopted the three-point line.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: It counted only for two points, as only the ABA had a three-point shot at the time

funFacts.text: Moments earlier, Dave DeBusschere had given New York a late lead, setting up West's desperation heave.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Dave DeBusschere made a shot with three seconds left to give New York a 102–100 edge

funFacts.text: The Knicks still won that overtime game despite West's heroics, holding the advantage in the series.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: the Knicks were able to win, 111–108

questions.prompt: Elgin Baylor led the Lakers to the Finals how many times, losing every one?

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: helped lead the team to the NBA Finals eight times, but the team lost each time.

funFacts.text: Baylor retired just before the Lakers embarked on their landmark winning streak and won the championship.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Baylor missed two historic achievements: the Lakers' first game afterwards began an NBA record 33-game win streak

funFacts.text: During an Army Reserve deployment, Baylor could join the Lakers only on weekend passes and flew coach to games.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: he could play for the Lakers only when on a weekend pass

funFacts.text: The Lakers were struggling financially when Baylor arrived; their owner credited him with keeping the franchise alive.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Baylor immediately exceeded expectations and ultimately saved the Lakers franchise
